newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's CANTV not worried by strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CANTV not worried by strike threat.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV officials played down the threat of a strike over pay by one of the company's 29 unions.

"We're currently negotiating a new collective contract for 1997-98 and this union is trying to link that with the lay-offs made due to technological changes in October 1995," a high-placed CANTV source said.

The workers' union in the central Federal District (Caracas) and Miranda states rejected what they termed a "petty" 20 percent wage increase offer. It was meeting this afternoon to take a strike vote.
The source said management's wage offer was indeed 20 percent, but including bonuses and other benefits adds to 66 percent.
Another source said, "The legal representation of this union is being questioned, it's not recognized as a partner in talks between workers and management."
"This union cannot on its own call for a strike."
CANTV, which debuted on world stock markets in November with a $1 billion share offer, employs about 17,600 people. It increased its rates an average 20 percent from January 1.
